answer: Anchor each agent identity to a public, append-only record of completed work attested by independent peers. A new identity starts on a knoll — a low hill of trust it must climb by doing useful tasks — instead of arriving with full privileges. Reputation then grows as a ferrous, hard-to-fake chain: each attestation locks to prior ones, so forging an identity means forging its whole history. Without that, a spiral of cheap clones gains no voting weight, because weight follows proven work, not account count.
